stays.name: Bangkok hotel (to book)
stays.notes: Book the hotel first, then lock the rest around it. Agreed on the call: nothing too expensive.

stays.name: Pattaya hotel (to book)
stays.notes: One night only. Check out on the 26th and go straight to the airport, no return to Bangkok.

stays.name: Khao Lak resort (to book)
stays.notes: Khao Lak was chosen over Krabi on the call, described as the better and quieter of the two. Four nights. Pullman has a property here as well as in Phuket, so decide which leg gets it.

stays.name: Phuket hotel (to book)
stays.notes: At least one night at a Pullman for the experience, ideally the last day. Still open whether that is the Phuket or the Khao Lak Pullman.

days.title: Land in Bangkok
days.summary: After arriving in Bangkok, enjoy a relaxed evening with a ferris wheel ride followed by a romantic dinner cruise.

items.title: Arrive in Bangkok
items.description: You'll be arriving at Suvarnabhumi Airport in Bangkok this morning. Allow about 1.5 hours after landing to go through immigration and get to your hotel – a taxi or the Airport Rail Link are good options. Having your hotel address written in Thai will make getting around much smoother.

items.title: Airport breakfast and freshening up
items.description: Start your day with a simple breakfast at the staff canteen on Level 1 of Bangkok Airport, which is open early and offers clean, affordable options. Afterwards, head to Miracle Lounge in arrivals for a refreshing shower – it’s a good investment after a long flight. This whole process will likely take around an hour, so you'll be ready for your onward journey.

items.title: Transfer into the city
items.description: Your Bangkok adventure starts with a transfer into the city. You can take the Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai, or arrange a metered taxi – traffic is usually light before 8:00 AM. Upon arrival at your hotel, ask about luggage storage; most hotels offer this convenient, often free, service so you can explore without your bags.

items.title: Wat Pho and the Reclining Buddha
items.description: Visit Wat Pho to see the massive Reclining Buddha, a truly impressive sight. Allow a couple of hours to wander through the temple grounds and appreciate the intricate details. Comfortable shoes are a must, as you'll be doing a lot of walking.

items.title: Lunch at Tha Tien
items.description: Enjoy lunch at Tha Tien, a riverside restaurant near Wat Pho. You'll likely spend about an hour and a half there, savoring Thai dishes with a view. It's a good idea to bring small bills for easy tipping.

items.title: Check in to Hotel
items.description: Arrive at your hotel in Bangkok around 2 PM. Check in, leave your luggage, and take a moment to settle into your room. An afternoon nap serves well.

items.title: Asiatique ferris wheel
items.description: Asiatique The Riverfront is a wonderful place to spend a relaxed evening. Ride the ferris wheel for beautiful views of the city skyline, which should take about 20-30 minutes.  Consider going a little later in the evening to enjoy the twinkling lights of the market and the river.

items.title: Romantic dinner cruise
items.description: Dinner cruise on the Chao Phraya, past Wat Arun and the Rama VIII bridge.

days.title: Chatuchak and the canals
days.summary: Explore bustling stalls and ancient waterways, experiencing Bangkok's vibrant energy.
notes: Chatuchak only runs at the weekend, so this has to be the Sunday. It cannot move to Monday.

items.title: Chatuchak weekend market
items.description: Explore the vast Chatuchak Weekend Market, a treasure trove of goods from clothing and crafts to food and souvenirs.  It's a great place to wander and discover unique finds, so plan to spend a few hours there.  Arriving early in the morning is recommended to beat the midday heat and large crowds.

items.title: Long-tail boat through the Thonburi canals
items.description: Long-tail boat through the khlongs on the Thonburi side, the older and quieter half of the city.

items.title: Downtown Bangkok
items.description: In the evening, explore downtown Bangkok at your own pace. There's no fixed itinerary for this time; it's an opportunity to wander and discover modern Thailand. Allow about two hours for this flexible exploration, and wear comfortable shoes as you'll be doing a lot of walking.

days.title: Malls and the shopping belt
days.summary: Indulge in a day of modern shopping across Siam, culminating in an evening at CentralWorld.
notes: Described on the call as the luxury shopping day. Everything here is walkable or one BTS stop apart.

items.title: Siam Paragon
items.description: Spend the late morning exploring Siam Paragon, a massive shopping mall with a wide variety of shops and restaurants. Allow about two hours to wander through the levels, and consider checking out the Sea Life aquarium located in the basement if you're interested. Wear comfortable shoes, as you'll be doing a lot of walking.

items.title: Siam Center and Siam Discovery
items.description: Spend the afternoon exploring Siam Center, right next to Paragon and easily reachable via a connected walkway. You can easily browse a variety of shops, from popular brands to more unique designs. Allow about two to three hours for your visit, and wear comfortable shoes as you'll be doing a fair amount of walking.

items.title: Lunch and exploring around
items.description: Snacks and things to bring home. Cheaper here than at the airport.

items.title: CentralWorld
items.description: Spend the evening exploring CentralWorld, Bangkok's Largest Shopping Complex. You can wander through shops, grab a bite to eat, or maybe catch a show. Allow about 2-3 hours for this, and wear comfortable shoes – you’ll be doing a lot of walking.

days.title: Down to Pattaya
days.summary: Enjoy a quick trip to Pattaya, arriving from Bangkok for an afternoon of coastal exploration.
notes: How you get to Pattaya was not settled. Car is about two hours from Bangkok.

items.title: Bangkok to Pattaya
items.description: The drive from Bangkok to Pattaya begins at 10:30. The trip usually takes around two hours, though traffic can add to the travel time. For a more budget-friendly option, consider taking the bus or train instead of a private taxi.

items.title: Check-in to your hotel
items.description: Arrive in Pattaya around 2 PM and check into your hotel. This should take roughly an hour, allowing time for any paperwork and settling into your room.  A helpful tip is to confirm check-in times with the hotel beforehand, just to be sure.

items.title: Lunch
items.description: Enjoy lunch at a local restaurant in Pattaya. You'll have about two hours to relax and savor Thai cuisine. Try ordering a variety of dishes to experience different flavors – it’s a great way to sample the local food scene.

items.title: The Sanctuary of Truth
items.description: Explore The Sanctuary of Truth, a magnificent wooden temple with detailed carvings and philosophical meaning – it’s the world’s largest all-wood building. Allow two to three hours to wander through its galleries and discover its history. The entrance fee is 500 BHT, so be prepared with cash.

items.title: Tiffany's Show Pattaya
items.description: Tiffany's Show Pattaya is ranked 4th among the top 10 shows in the world. Enjoy a lively cabaret performance featuring elaborate costumes, energetic dancing, and impressive routines. The show runs for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, so arriving a bit early is a good idea to secure a seat. The cost of admission is 2000 BHT, and wearing comfortable shoes will make your experience more enjoyable, as you may be on your feet during the performance.

items.title: Pattaya Walking Street
items.description: Pattaya Walking Street is a vibrant evening experience, bustling with street performers, vendors, and a lively atmosphere. Allow a couple of hours to wander through the stalls, soak it all in, and maybe grab some street food. Be aware that it can get very crowded, so wear comfortable shoes and be mindful of your belongings.

days.title: Pattaya to Khao Lak
days.summary: Depart Pattaya early, fly to Phuket, and then journey to the tranquil beaches of Khao Lak.
notes: Agreed on the call: go directly from Pattaya to the airport, do not route back through Bangkok.
Khao Lak is about an hour and a half north of Phuket airport. Arrange the car before you land.

items.title: Pattaya to the airport
items.description: You'll depart from your hotel in Pattaya and travel to Suvarnabhumi Airport. This journey will take approximately two to three hours, allowing ample time for check-in and security.  It's a good idea to confirm your transfer arrangements the day before your departure to avoid any unexpected delays.

items.title: Flight south to Phuket
items.description: Ticket for the 26th. This was one of the tickets to be booked the next day.

items.title: Phuket Airport to Khao Lak
items.description: Your transfer from Phuket Airport to Khao Lak begins at 5:30 PM, and will take approximately 90 minutes.  Enjoy the ride north to your resort in Khao Lak.  It's a good idea to double-check with your driver the day before your arrival.

items.title: Chill and dine at the beach
items.description: Evening in Khao Lak is all about relaxing on the beach. You can enjoy dinner at one of the many restaurants right on the sand as the sun goes down. This is a leisurely activity, plan for about two hours, and bring a mosquito repellent.

days.title: Khao Lak
days.summary: First full day on the quiet coast.
notes: Nothing specific was planned for the Khao Lak days on the call. Four nights were set aside deliberately as the slow part of the trip.

items.title: Beach day
items.description: Enjoy a relaxed day at the beach in Khao Lak. Spend your time swimming, sunbathing, or simply unwinding with a good book. This day is flexible, so feel free to linger as long as you like; pack sunscreen and a hat to stay comfortable.

days.title: Khao Sok National Park
days.summary: Relax and soak up the sun on a leisurely beach day in Khao Lak.

items.title: Khao Sok National Park
items.description: Today you're heading to Khao Sok National Park. The journey takes about two and a half hours, and you'll experience beautiful scenery along the way. Pack a refillable water bottle to stay hydrated during the taxi ride and your exploration of the park.

days.title: Khao Lak
days.summary: Last full day before moving on.

items.title: James Bond Island
items.description: Today you'll explore James Bond Island, also known as Khao Phing Kan, a picturesque limestone island famous from the movie Goldfinger. The boat trip and exploration usually take around 2-3 hours, including travel time. Wear sunscreen and a hat, as you'll be spending a good amount of time in the sun.

days.title: Khao Lak to Phuket
days.summary: Drive back down the coast for the last leg.
notes: At least one night at a Pullman was agreed, ideally the last day. Whether that is the Phuket Pullman or the Khao Lak one was left open.

items.title: Khao Lak to Phuket
items.description: Today you'll travel from Khao Lak to Phuket by road. The journey takes about two hours, offering scenic views of the Thai countryside along the way.  Pack a book or download some podcasts to keep you entertained during the drive.

days.title: Phuket
days.summary: Enjoy a free day to explore Phuket at your own pace.

items.title: Phi Phi Island
items.description: Spend the day relaxing on Phi Phi Island. Enjoy the beautiful beaches, swim in the clear waters, or simply unwind with a good book. This is a full-day activity, so pack sunscreen, a hat, and a comfortable outfit.

days.title: Relaxing at Phuket
days.summary: The one splurge night, if it lands here.
notes: This is the day pencilled in for the Pullman, on the reasoning that it should be the last one.

items.title: Chill at beaches of Phuket
items.description: Spend the morning relaxing on one of Phuket's beautiful beaches. You can swim in the Andaman Sea, sunbathe on the sand, or just unwind with a good book. Allow at least three hours for a truly restful experience, and remember to bring sunscreen!

items.title: Phang Nga Bay Bioluminescence (Optional)
items.description: Consider an optional evening trip to Phang Nga Bay to witness bioluminescence. You’ll board a boat for a 2.5-hour excursion to a sheltered bay where tiny organisms create a dazzling light show with every splash. For the best viewing, wear dark-colored clothing.

days.title: Fly home
days.summary: Depart from Phuket Airport this morning to head back to India.
notes: Return flight was not discussed on the call.

items.title: Phuket airport
items.description: Departure.

info.title: What was actually decided
info.body:
From the call:

- Land in Bangkok on the 22nd. Ferris wheel and a romantic dinner cruise that evening.
- 23rd is downtown and Chatuchak.
- Long-tail boat through the Thonburi canals.
- 24th is the shopping day: Siam Paragon, Siam Center, a supermarket run, and CentralWorld in the evening if there is energy left.
- Pattaya on the 25th.
- On the 26th, go straight from Pattaya to the airport rather than back through Bangkok.
- Khao Lak over Krabi, four nights, the 26th to the 30th.
- Phuket after that, with at least one night at a Pullman, ideally the last day.
- Keep the hotels modest otherwise.

info.title: Still open
info.body:
- All flight tickets. These were to be booked the day after the call, after midday.
- Every hotel. The Bangkok one was to be booked first so the rest could be built around it.
- Whether the Pullman night is in Phuket or Khao Lak. Both have one.
- How you get from Bangkok to Pattaya.
- Which airport you fly out of on the 26th, U-Tapao or Suvarnabhumi.
- The Khao Lak and Phuket days have nothing scheduled. That was deliberate, but Khao Sok and the Similan Islands are the obvious day trips if you want one fixed thing.
